title.en: Strike over high fuel prices paralyses transport in Kenya
title.zh: 肯尼亚因高燃料价格罢工导致交通瘫痪

summary.en: Key roads in Kenya have remained largely empty, and some schools have asked students to stay at home due to a strike protesting high fuel prices.
summary.zh: 肯尼亚因抗议高燃料价格的罢工，主要道路大都空无一人，一些学校已要求学生留在家中。

body.en:
Thousands of Kenyan commuters have been stranded and businesses paralysed as public transport operators went on a nationwide strike to protest against recent increases in the cost fuel.

Key roads in the capital Nairobi remained largely empty, forcing some commuters to walk to work, with other parts of the country also affected by the transport crisis. Businesses in parts of Nairobi remained shut and schools asked students to stay at home.

Protesters have been barricading roads and lighting fires on the roads as the protests continue.

The strike comes days after the authorities raised petroleum prices to record levels, with costs increasing by more than 20%.

Kenya, like many other African countries, relies heavily on fuel imports from the Gulf, a supply route disrupted by the US-Israel conflict with Iran that began on 28 February. Even though a ceasefire has been declared, fuel prices have remained high as the Strait of Hormuz, where a fifth of the world's oil passes through, is still blocked.

In parts of Nairobi and elsewhere across the country, police clashed with protesters, using tear gas to disperse them. This came amid reports of demonstrators stopping and harassing some motorists.

Ahead of the strike, the police assured Kenyans that security measures would be in place and warned against any disruptive conduct.

The association representing transport operators had earlier urged all vehicle users, including private motorists, public transport buses (locally known as matatus) and truckers, to stay off the roads as part of a coordinated shutdown.

"This action is not only for transport operators, but for every Kenyan citizen," the Transport Sector Alliance (TSA) said in a statement.

The alliance has accused the government of not doing enough to shield Kenyans from the rising fuel prices, amid a broader high cost-of-living crisis.

It has called for the reversal of the price increases announced last week, and for fuel prices to be reduced by about 35%.

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (Epra) on Thursday raised prices to a high of 242 shillings ($1.8; £1.4) a litre for diesel and petrol to $1.65.

Treasury Minister John Mbadi told local NTV station on Monday that the increase in fuel prices was "unfortunate" and acknowledged that it was hurting the economy.

He however said the strike was "completely uncalled for" and the government would only make decisions that are "informed and not emotional".

The high cost of fuel is being blamed for increases in the price of food and other basic goods and services, with public service vehicles already raising commuter fares.

Last month, the government cut VAT on fuel from 16% to 8% until July but there have been calls for it to do more.
body.zh: 由于公共交通运营商举行全国性罢工以抗议最近燃油成本上涨，数千名肯尼亚通勤者陷入困境，企业陷入瘫痪。 首都内罗毕的主要道路仍然基本上空无一人，迫使一些通勤者步行上班，该国其他地区也受到了交通危机的影响。内罗毕部分地区的企业仍然关闭，学校要求学生呆在家里。 随着抗议活动的继续，抗议者一直在道路上设置路障并点火。 此次罢工发生几天前，当局将石油价格提高到创纪录水平，成本上涨了 20% 以上。 与许多其他非洲国家一样，肯尼亚严重依赖从海湾进口燃料，这条供应路线因 2 月 28 日开始的美以与伊朗冲突而中断。尽管已经宣布停火，但由于全球五分之一的石油经过的霍尔木兹海峡仍然被封锁，燃油价格仍然居高不下。 在内罗毕部分地区和全国其他地方，警察与抗议者发生冲突，使用催泪瓦斯驱散他们。据报道，示威者拦截并骚扰了一些驾车者。 罢工前，警方向肯尼亚人保证，将采取安全措施，并警告不要进行任何破坏性行为。 代表运输运营商的协会早些时候敦促所有车辆使用者，包括私人驾车者、公共交通巴士（当地称为马塔图斯）和卡车司机，不要上路，作为协调关闭的一部分。 运输部门联盟（TSA）在一份声明中表示：“这一行动不仅针对运输运营商，而且针对每一位肯尼亚公民。” 该联盟指责政府在更广泛的高生活成本危机中没有采取足够措施来保护肯尼亚人免受燃油价格上涨的影响。 它呼吁扭转上周宣布的涨价政策，并将燃油价格降低约35%。 能源和石油管理局 (Epra) 周四将柴油价格提高至每升 242 先令（1.8 美元；1.4 英镑），汽油价格提高至每升 1.65 美元。 财政部长约翰·姆巴迪周一对当地 NTV 电视台表示，燃油价格上涨是“不幸的”，并承认这正在损害经济。 不过他表示，罢工“完全没有必要”，政府只会在“知情而不是情绪化”的情况下做出决定。 食品和其他基本商品和服务价格上涨被归咎于燃料成本高昂，公共服务车辆已经提高了通勤费用。 上个月，政府将燃油增值税从 16% 削减至 8%，直至 7 月，但有人呼吁政府采取更多措施。

reflection.zh: 当燃料等基本生活成本急剧上涨时，许多人的日常生活会变得沉重，导致社会普遍混乱。这种情况提醒我们，圣经呼吁领袖以公义和正直治理，确保所有公民的福祉。它突显了经济压力对社区的深远影响，以及对富有同情心的领导力的需求。

verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: At least six Americans exposed to Ebola during DR Congo outbreak
title.zh: 至少六名美国人在刚果民主共和国埃博拉疫情中接触病毒

summary.en: Officials report that at least six Americans were exposed to Ebola during an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with one individual reportedly experiencing symptoms.
summary.zh: 据媒体报道，至少有六名美国人在刚果民主共和国的埃博拉疫情中接触了病毒，其中一人已出现症状。

body.en:
At least six Americans have been exposed to the Ebola virus during a deadly outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, sources have told CBS News, the BBC's US partner.

The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared the outbreak as an international emergency, with the DR Congo's health ministry reporting around 350 suspected cases and 91 deaths.

One American is believed to be have symptoms, with three others said to have faced a high-risk contact or exposure. It is unclear whether any have been infected.

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was supporting the "safe withdrawal of a small number of Americans who are directly affected", but did not confirm how many.

The current strain of Ebola is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, for which there are no approved drugs or vaccines.

There are also two confirmed cases and one death in Uganda, according to the CDC.

The US government is reportedly looking to arrange transport for the small group of Americans in DR Congo to a safe quarantine location, a source told health news site STAT.

Quoting a source, the site adds that the group could be taken to a US military base in Germany, though this has not been confirmed.

During a press conference on Sunday, the CDC declined to answer direct questions about the US citizens reportedly affected, adding that the risk to the US remained low.

The US has also issued a Level Four travel advisory - its most severe level - warning against travel to the DR Congo.

The WHO has said the outbreak in DR Congo's eastern Ituri province is a public health emergency of international concern, but did not meet the criteria of a pandemic.

The agency has also warned it could potentially be "a much larger outbreak" than what is currently being detected and reported, with significant risk of local and regional spread.

More than 28,600 people were infected by Ebola during the 2014-2016 outbreak in West Africa, the largest outbreak of the virus since its discovery in 1976.

The disease spread to a number of countries within and outside of West Africa, including Guinea, Sierra Leone, the United States, the United Kingdom and Italy, killing 11,325 people.

Jean Kaseya, director general of Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, warned that in the absence of vaccines and effective medicines people should follow public health measures, including the guidance about handling the funerals of those who have died from the disease.

"We don't want people infected because of funerals," he told the BBC World Service's Newsday programme.

Community funerals, where people helped wash the bodies of their loved ones, contributed to many people becoming infected in the earlier stages of the big outbreak more than a decade ago.

reflection.en: News of disease outbreaks can bring anxiety and concern for those affected. In such moments, the biblical call to pray for the sick reminds us of our shared humanity and the power of compassionate intercession. We hold in prayer all who are vulnerable to illness and those working to provide care and healing.
reflection.zh: 疾病爆发的消息常会带来焦虑和担忧。在这样的时刻，圣经呼吁我们为病人祷告，提醒我们共同的人性和怜悯代祷的力量。我们为所有易受疾病侵袭的人以及那些致力于提供护理和医治的人献上祷告。

verse.textEn: Is anyone among you sick? Let them call the elders of the church to pray over them.
verse.textZh: 你们中间有病了的呢，他就该请教会的长老来；他们可以奉主的名用油抹他，为他祷告。

title.en: Lammy dismisses Streeting’s call for UK to rejoin EU as ‘sixth form’ debating position – UK politics live
title.zh: 拉米驳斥斯特里廷关于英国重新加入欧盟的呼吁为“高中生”辩论立场——英国政治直播

summary.en: The UK Deputy Prime Minister dismissed a colleague's call for the UK to rejoin the EU as an immature debating position, warning that weeks of internal debate on the issue and Labour leadership would alienate the public and benefit rival parties.
summary.zh: 英国副首相拉米驳斥了一位同事关于英国重新加入欧盟的呼吁，称其为“高中生”式的辩论立场。他警告说，数周围绕欧盟和工党领导层的内部辩论将疏远公众，并对竞争对手政党有利。

body.en: Deputy PM says the public will not forgive weeks of internal debate on the EU and Labour leadership, warning it will play into Reform’s hands Jessica Elgot is the Guardian’s deputy political editor. Keir Starmer has been visiting Labour HQ this morning and speaking to staff, saying the party needs to offer “a bit more hope.” I just wanted to come here to Labour party headquarters to say a big thank you to you. The election results were not the ones that we wanted, they were really tough. But you worked your socks off. It’s not been easy circumstances in the last 10 days. But you have just got on with the job that we asked you to do. If you look at just some of the figures that came out last week. We had growth figures that were the best in the G7. That’s because of the hard work that we’ve done in government. On the economy we’ve got ourselves into a good position, having inherited a real basket case from the last government. The NHS figures were really good, which again vindicates what we did, which was invest in the NHS, which is what we said we would do. And that’s on top of all the other things … The Employment Rights Act. The biggest upgrade in renters’ rights in a generation. And then of course all the work that we are doing around child poverty, of which I am really proud. What a game changer that will be for a whole generation and will be measured for years and years to come because the children will feel the impact for the rest of their lives. They will have chances they wouldn’t otherwise have had. The election results tell us that people are frustrated, they don’t feel that their lives have changed quickly enough. We need to build up the urgency of what we do. We need a bit more hope in there. And we need to remember at all times what we are here to do. We were elected to government to serve the people of this country. And I remind myself every day that in July 2024 millions of people voted for us to come into government, to get on with the job, to govern, and to bring about the change that they want. So I am focused on the job that I was asked to do, which is to serve my country and to carry out my duties as prime minister of this country. Delivering for the very many people who voted us into office, who are saying, ‘just get on with it, get on with the job, get on with the change that I need to see in my life’. And that is what I am going to be doing. We now have an important by-election coming up. It is Labour versus Reform. We will know very shortly who the candidate is. Whoever they are I am going to support them 100% and I want every member, everyone in our movement, to support them. A Labour candidate to beat Reform. That is the fight that we are in. body.zh: 副首相表示，公众不会原谅针对欧盟和工党领导层持续数周的内部辩论，并警告称这将落入改革的手中。基尔·斯塔默（Keir Starmer）今天早上访问了工党总部并与工作人员交谈，称该党需要提供“更多一点希望”。我只是想来到工党总部向你们表示深深的感谢。选举结果不是我们想要的，真的很艰难。但你已经竭尽全力了。过去 10 天的情况并不轻松。但你刚刚开始完成我们要求你做的工作。如果你只看上周公布的一些数据。我们的增长数据是七国集团中最好的。这是因为我们在政府中所做的辛勤工作。在经济方面，我们已经处于有利地位，从上届政府那里继承了真正的困境。 NHS 的数据非常好，这再次证明了我们所做的事情是正确的，那就是对 NHS 的投资，这就是我们所说的我们会做的。这是最重要的……《就业权利法》。这是一代人以来租房者权利最大的升级。当然，还有我们围绕儿童贫困所做的所有工作，我对此感到非常自豪。这对于整整一代人来说是多么大的改变，并将在未来的岁月里得到衡量，因为孩子们将在余生中感受到这种影响。他们将拥有本来没有的机会。选举结果告诉我们，人们感到沮丧，他们觉得自己的生活改变得不够快。我们需要增强我们所做工作的紧迫性。我们需要多一点希望。我们需要时刻记住我们来这里的目的。我们当选政府是为了为这个国家的人民服务。我每天都提醒自己，2024 年 7 月，数百万人投票支持我们进入政府、继续工作、治理并实现他们想要的变革。因此，我专注于我被要求做的工作，即为我的国家服务并履行我作为这个国家总理的职责。为那些投票让我们当选的很多人提供服务，他们说，“继续做下去，继续工作，继续我生活中需要看到的改变”。这就是我要做的事情。我们现在即将举行重要的补选。这是工党与改革的斗争。我们很快就会知道候选人是谁。无论他们是谁，我都会百分百支持他们，我希望我们运动中的每个成员、每个人都支持他们。击败改革的工党候选人。这就是我们正在进行的战斗。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Political life often involves vigorous debate, but the wisdom of collective decision-making lies in valuing diverse perspectives and seeking common ground. When internal disagreements become dismissive or prolonged, they can undermine public trust and weaken a shared purpose.
reflection.zh: 政治生活常涉及激烈的辩论，但集体决策的智慧在于珍视多元观点并寻求共同点。当内部意见分歧变得轻蔑或旷日持久时，它们可能会损害公众信任并削弱共同目标。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Dr Hook co-frontman Dennis Locorriere dies aged 76

body.en: Singer took lead vocal on UK No 1 When You’re in Love With a Beautiful Woman, and had numerous other transatlantic hits Dennis Locorriere, the guitarist and singer with the chart-topping soft rock band Dr Hook, has died aged 76. A statement from his management company said he died on Saturday “after a long and courageous battle with kidney disease … Dennis faced his illness with remarkable strength, dignity, and resilience throughout, and remained deeply cherished by all who knew him”. body.zh: 歌手在英国排名第一的《当你爱上一个美丽的女人》中担任主唱，并在跨大西洋创作了许多其他热门歌曲。 排行榜冠军软摇滚乐队 Dr Hook 的吉他手兼歌手丹尼斯·洛科里尔 (Dennis Locorriere) 去世，享年 76 岁。他的经纪公司的一份声明称，他“在与肾病进行了长期而勇敢的斗争后于周六去世……丹尼斯自始至终以非凡的力量、尊严和韧性面对疾病，并受到所有认识他的人的深深怀念”。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news of Dennis Locorriere's passing marks the end of a significant musical journey, reminding us of the lives well-lived and the legacies left behind. For those who dedicate their lives to their craft, there comes a time when the race is finished, and their work is complete. We reflect on the impact of their contributions and the enduring mark they...
reflection.zh: 丹尼斯·洛科里尔去世的消息标志着一段重要音乐旅程的终结，提醒我们那些活出精彩人生并留下遗产的人。对于那些将生命奉献给其事业的人来说，总有一天，赛程结束，他们的工作也随之完成。我们反思他们所做贡献的影响，以及他们给世界留下的持久印记。

verse.textEn: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
verse.textZh: 那美好的仗我已经打过了，当跑的路我已经跑尽了，所信的道我已经守住了。

title.en: Middle East crisis live: Trump warns ‘clock is ticking’ for Iran to reach peace deal
title.zh: 中东危机：特朗普警告伊朗“时间不多”以达成和平协议

summary.en: The US president has issued a warning to Iran, stating that the country faces severe consequences if a peace agreement is not reached soon. This comes amidst rising tensions, with the UAE blaming Iran or its proxies for a drone strike near a nuclear plant, and Iran announcing new management for the Strait of Hormuz.
summary.zh: 美国总统向伊朗发出警告，称如果不能尽快达成和平协议，该国将面临严重后果。此前，中东地区紧张局势加剧，阿联酋指责伊朗或其代理人对核电站附近发动无人机袭击，而伊朗则宣布将对霍尔木兹海峡实施新的管理。

body.en: US president says there ‘won’t be anything left’ of country if it doesn’t come to an agreement UAE blames Iran or its proxies for drone strike fire near nuclear plant Iran’s top security body has announced the formation of a new body to manage the strait of Hormuz, which Tehran has effectively closed to countries it deems hostile to it – and wants to charge ships to traverse. On its official X account, the Supreme national security council shared a post for the Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) saying it would provide “real‑time updates on the Hormuz Strait operations and latest developments”. In such moments, we hold onto the hope that 雅伟 is the one who ultimately "makes wars cease to the ends of the earth." May leaders and nations seek paths that lead to the breaking of weapons and the burning of shields, rather than...
reflection.zh: 中东地区日益加剧的紧张局势和严峻后果的警告，提醒我们冲突的破坏性潜力。在这样的时刻，我们紧紧抓住希望，相信雅伟是那位最终“使战争止息，直到地极”的神。愿各国领袖和国家寻求能使武器折断、战车焚烧的道路，而非将其投入使用。

verse.textEn: He makes wars cease to the ends of the earth; he breaks the bow and shatters the spear.
verse.textZh: 他止息刀兵，直到地极；他折弓断枪。

title.en: Trump’s immigration crackdown could cost up to $479bn in lost taxes over 10 years
title.zh: 特朗普的移民打击措施可能导致十年内损失高达4790亿美元的税收

summary.en: A proposed immigration crackdown by the Trump administration, including IRS data sharing with immigration authorities and ICE raids, could lead to a loss of up to $479 billion in tax revenue over the next decade. This is due to undocumented individuals potentially avoiding tax filings out of fear.
summary.zh: 特朗普政府提议的移民打击措施，包括美国国税局与移民机构共享数据以及移民及海关执法局的突袭行动，可能导致未来十年内美国损失高达4790亿美元的税收。这是因为无证移民可能出于恐惧而避免报税。

body.en: Proposed IRS data sharing with immigration authorities and ICE raids have made filing risky for those who are undocumented The Trump administration’s immigration crackdown could cause the US to potentially lose up to $479bn in lost tax revenue over the the next 10 years, with enforcement deterring undocumented workers from filing their taxes this year, according to tax experts. Tax advisers say major changes, including proposed data sharing with immigration enforcement, have made filing taxes risky for undocumented immigrants. Tax benefits for immigrant parents have also been removed, further removing incentive to file taxes at all. Continue reading...
body.zh: 拟议中的 IRS 与移民当局共享数据以及 ICE 突击搜查使无证工人报税面临风险 税务专家称，特朗普政府的移民打击行动可能导致美国在未来 10 年可能损失高达 4790 亿美元的税收收入，而执法行动将阻止无证工人今年报税。税务顾问表示，重大变化，包括拟议与移民执法部门共享数据，使无证移民报税面临风险。移民父母的税收优惠也被取消，进一步消除了报税的动力。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Policies that instill fear in foreign residents, even those undocumented, can have far-reaching consequences, impacting both individuals and the broader economy. This reminds us of the ancient call to treat the stranger among us with dignity and fairness, remembering our shared human experience. Such an approach fosters trust and can lead to more stable and...
reflection.zh: 针对外国居民的政策，即使是针对无证移民的政策，如果制造恐惧，可能会产生深远的影响，波及个人和整体经济。这提醒我们，要以尊严和公平对待我们中间的陌生人，铭记我们共同的人类经历。这种做法能培养信任，并为所有人带来更稳定和繁荣的社区。

verse.textEn: When a foreigner resides among you in your land, do not mistreat them. The foreigner residing among you must be treated as your native-born. Love them as yourself, for you were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Israeli forces boarding Gaza-bound flotilla near Cyprus, activists say
title.zh: 活动人士称，以色列军队在塞浦路斯附近登上驶往加沙的船队

summary.en: Live broadcasts from the Global Sumud flotilla show commandos boarding several boats trying to breach the Gaza maritime blockade.
summary.zh: “全球坚韧”船队的直播显示，突击队员登上了几艘试图突破加沙海上封锁的船只。

body.en:
Pro-Palestinian activists say Israeli forces are intercepting a flotilla of more than 50 boats carrying aid for Gaza in international waters west of Cyprus.

The Global Sumud Flotilla (GSF) said its fleet was being boarded in what it called an illegal act of piracy about 250 nautical miles (460km) from Gaza, which is under an Israeli maritime blockade. Its video stream showed armed commandos climbing onto several boats.

There was no immediate comment from Israel. Earlier, its foreign ministry described the flotilla as "a provocation for the sake of provocation" and said it involved "two violent Turkish groups".

Last month, Israeli forces intercepted 22 boats from the same flotilla near Crete.

In that incident, about 175 activists on board were detained, all but two of whom were released on the Greek island the next day following widespread international condemnation.

Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian national Thiago Ávila were taken back to Israel for questioning and deported after spending 10 days in custody.

The flotilla's remaining boats then sailed to the Turkish port of Marmaris, where about 50 boats departed last Thursday and headed south-east towards Gaza.

Activists on board said they needed to reach Gaza to provide much-needed aid to Palestinians in the territory, where living conditions are dire and most of the 2.1 million population is displaced, despite the ceasefire agreed by Israel and Hamas seven months ago.

Israel's foreign ministry said it would not allow any breach of the maritime blockade on Gaza, which it insisted was lawful, and described Gaza as "flooded with aid".

The UN said last week that humanitarian operations continued to be undermined by restrictions on the import of critical spare parts, back-up generators and other equipment, as well as shortages of essential inputs, including fuel and engine oil.

It also said only 86% of the humanitarian supplies initially approved by Israeli authorities for entry into Gaza were ultimately offloaded at border crossings. The remaining supplies were returned to their points of origin.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Israel responded by launching a military campaign in Gaza, during which more than 72,760 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry.
body.zh: 亲巴勒斯坦活动人士表示，以色列军队正在塞浦路斯以西的国际水域拦截一支由 50 多艘船只组成的向加沙运送援助物资的船队。 全球苏姆德船队 (GSF) 表示，其船队在距离加沙约 250 海里（460 公里）处被登上，这是一种非法海盗行为，加沙目前处于以色列海上封锁之下。其视频流显示武装突击队爬上几艘船。 以色列没有立即发表评论。早些时候，土耳其外交部称这支船队是“为了挑衅而挑衅”，并表示它涉及“两个土耳其暴力组织”。 上个月，以色列军队在克里特岛附近拦截了同一支船队的 22 艘船只。 在那次事件中，船上约 175 名活动人士被拘留，在国际社会广泛谴责后，第二天除两人外，其余人均在希腊岛上被释放。 西班牙国民赛义夫·阿布·凯谢克 (Saif Abu Keshek) 和巴西国民蒂亚戈·阿维拉 (Thiago Ávila) 在被拘留 10 天后被带回以色列接受审问并被驱逐出境。 随后，该船队的剩余船只驶往土耳其马尔马里斯港，大约 50 艘船只于上周四出发，向东南方向驶向加沙。 船上的活动人士表示，他们需要抵达加沙，为该地区的巴勒斯坦人提供急需的援助，尽管以色列和哈马斯在七个月前达成了停火协议，但那里的生活条件十分恶劣，210万人口中的大多数人都流离失所。 以色列外交部表示，不会允许任何违反对加沙海上封锁的行为，并坚称这是合法的，并称加沙“充满了援助”。 联合国上周表示，由于关键备件、备用发电机和其他设备的进口限制，以及燃料和机油等基本投入的短缺，人道主义行动继续受到损害。 报告还表示，以色列当局最初批准进入加沙的人道主义物资中，只有 86% 最终在边境口岸卸下。剩余物资已返回原产地。 加沙战争是由哈马斯领导的 2023 年 10 月 7 日对以色列南部的袭击引发的，当时约 1,200 人被杀，另有 251 人被劫为人质。 作为回应，以色列在加沙发动了军事行动，据哈马斯控制的该地区卫生部称，此次行动已造成 72,760 多人死亡。

reflection.en: The news of forces boarding a flotilla highlights the persistent barriers and deep-seated divisions that create hostility between peoples. In such moments, we are reminded of the profound need for peace that transcends human-made walls. Scripture points to a hope where such dividing walls are broken down, allowing for unity and understanding.
reflection.zh: 部队登上船队的消息，凸显了造成民族间敌意的持续障碍和根深蒂固的分歧。在这样的时刻，我们被提醒对超越人造藩篱的和平有着深刻的需求。圣经指向一个希望，在那里，这样的隔阂之墙被拆毁，带来合一与理解。

verse.textEn: For he himself is our peace, who has made the two groups one and has destroyed the barrier, the dividing wall of hostility.
verse.textZh: 因他使我们和睦，将两下合而为一，拆毁了中间隔断的墙。

title.en: Trump warns 'clock is ticking' for Iran as peace progress stalls
title.zh: 特朗普警告伊朗“时间不多了”，和平进程陷入停滞

summary.en: Iran announced on Monday that it had responded to the latest US proposal, indicating that diplomatic exchanges with Washington are ongoing despite stalled progress in peace talks.
summary.zh: 伊朗周一表示已回应美国最新提案，并称与华盛顿的交流仍在继续，尽管和平进程陷入停滞。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has warned Iran the "clock is ticking" as talks to bring the war to an end have stalled.

"They better get moving, FAST, or there won't be anything left of them," he wrote on his Truth Social platform. "TIME IS OF THE ESSENCE!"

The message came as the president spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday, the Times of Israel reported, citing Netanyahu's office.

On Monday Iran said it had responded to the latest US proposal and that exchanges with Washington were continuing through Pakistani mediators.

"As we announced yesterday, our concerns were conveyed to the American side," the country's foreign ministry spokesperson said at a media briefing, the AFP reported.

Iranian media earlier reported the US had failed to make any concrete concessions to Tehran, with the semi-official Mehr news agency saying a lack of compromise would lead to an "impasse in the negotiations".

Trump's message echoed his threat that a "whole civilisation" would die unless Iran agreed to a deal to end the war, shortly before the ceasefire was announced in early April.

The president warned earlier this week that truce was on "massive life support" after rejecting Tehran's demands, labelling them "totally unacceptable". Esmail Baghaei, an Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson, then insisted they were "responsible" and "generous".

According to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency, the Iranian asks included an immediate end to the war on all fronts - a reference to the continued Israeli attacks against Iran-supported Hezbollah in Lebanon - a halt to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, and guarantees of no further attacks on Iran.

They also reportedly included a demand for compensation for war damage and an emphasis on Iranian sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz.

Iran's semi-official Fars news agency said on Sunday that Washington had set five conditions in response to Tehran's proposal.

They reportedly included a demand that Iran keep only one nuclear site in operation and transfer its stockpile of highly enriched uranium to the US.

Trump suggested on Friday that he would accept a 20-year suspension by Iran of its nuclear programme - a major sticking point between the two countries - in what appeared to be confirmation of a shift in position away from a demand for a total end to it.

Israeli and US forces began massive air strikes on Iran on 28 February. The ceasefire meant to facilitate talks has largely been observed despite occasional exchanges of fire.

Iran has also continued to control the Strait of Hormuz, effectively closing the vital waterway through which around 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas travels.

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普警告伊朗，随着结束战争的谈判陷入僵局，“时间正在流逝”。 他在自己的真相社交平台上写道：“他们最好尽快行动，否则他们将一无所有。” “时间就是生命！” 据《以色列时报》援引内塔尼亚胡办公室的报道，总统周日与以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡通话时发出了这一信息。 伊朗周一表示，已对美国的最新提议做出回应，并通过巴基斯坦调解人继续与华盛顿进行交流。 据法新社报道，该国外交部发言人在媒体吹风会上表示：“正如我们昨天宣布的那样，我们的担忧已转达给美方。” 伊朗媒体早些时候报道称，美国未能向德黑兰做出任何具体让步，半官方的迈赫尔通讯社表示，缺乏妥协将导致“谈判陷入僵局”。 特朗普的信息呼应了他的威胁，即除非伊朗在四月初宣布停火前不久同意达成结束战争的协议，否则“整个文明”将会消亡。 总统本周早些时候警告说，在拒绝德黑兰的要求后，停战将依赖于“巨大的生命支持”，并称这些要求“完全不可接受”。伊朗外交部发言人埃斯梅尔·巴格哈伊随后坚称他们是“负责任的”和“慷慨的”。 据伊朗半官方的塔斯尼姆通讯社报道，伊朗的要求包括立即结束各条战线的战争——指的是以色列对伊朗支持的黎巴嫩真主党的持续袭击——停止美国对伊朗港口的海上封锁，并保证不再对伊朗发动进一步的袭击。 据报道，这些协议还包括要求赔偿战争损失，并强调伊朗对霍尔木兹海峡的主权。 伊朗半官方法尔斯通讯社周日表示，华盛顿针对德黑兰的提议提出了五项条件。 据报道，其中包括一项要求，要求伊朗只保留一处核设施仍在运行，并将其高浓缩铀库存转移到美国。 特朗普周五表示，他将接受伊朗暂停其核计划20年的决定——这是两国之间的一个主要症结所在——这似乎证实了其立场的转变，不再要求彻底结束核计划。 2月28日，以色列和美国军队开始对伊朗进行大规模空袭。尽管偶尔发生交火，但旨在促进谈判的停火协议基本上得到遵守。 伊朗还继续控制霍尔木兹海峡，有效关闭了世界上约 20% 的石油和液化天然气运输的重要水道。 伊朗称此举是为了报复美国和以色列的袭击，此举引发...

reflection.en: The news of stalled peace progress reminds us of the constant human endeavor to live at peace, even amidst complex international relations. This verse encourages us to pursue peace diligently, recognizing that while we cannot control all outcomes, our own efforts to foster dialogue and understanding remain vital. It calls for persistent engagement, as far...
reflection.zh: 和平进程停滞的消息提醒我们，在复杂的国际关系中，人类持续努力寻求和平。这节经文鼓励我们勤勉地追求和平，认识到虽然我们无法掌控所有结果，但我们促进对话和理解的自身努力至关重要。它呼吁我们尽力持续参与，以寻求和谐。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Escaped tiger shot by German police after attacking man
title.zh: 逃脱老虎袭击男子后被德国警方击毙

summary.en: A tiger that escaped from a local trainer's facility in Germany attacked a man before being shot by police. The trainer is known as Germany's "Tiger Queen."
summary.zh: 据当地媒体报道，一只从当地驯兽师卡门·赞德（Carmen Zander，也被称为德国“老虎女王”）的设施中逃脱的老虎，在袭击一名男子后被德国警方击毙。

body.en:
An escaped tiger believed to be owned by Germany's "Tiger Queen" has been shot dead by police after attacking one of its keepers.

Police told the BBC a 72-year-old man was seriously injured after being attacked on Sunday while he was inside the animal's enclosure, located in a privately-owned facility on the outskirts of the German city of Leipzig.

The tiger escaped the enclosure and was found shortly after by armed police, who shot and killed the animal.

The site of the enclosure is believed to be owned by controversial trainer and private owner Carmen Zander, who describes herself as Germany's "Tiger Queen".

The animal was one of eight big cats kept at the industrial site near the German town of Schkeuditz, according to local media.

In a statement to the BBC, police said officers shot the animal, a male tiger, to eliminate any further risk to the public.

It added that the local police department received the emergency call at around 12:50 local time (11:50 BST) on Sunday, with officers arriving at the scene quickly.

No other animals have escaped from the site and police have planned a drone search to ensure it is fully secure.

District Mayor Thomas Druskat called for the other animals to be relocated and told local media it was "unthinkable" what could have happened if anyone else had been harmed.

Nearby residents told the Deutsche Presse-Agentur (DPA) that the incident was "terrible and worrying", with one claiming the animals were not kept in appropriate conditions.

Animal rights charity Peta called on the government to act, telling DPA that stricter rules needed to be put in place to protect privately-owned animals.

According to a website using Zander's name and nickname, the trainer holds "unforgettable" and "one-of-a-kind" tiger petting events open to the public.

The website says visitors can pay to pet the "250kg powerhouses" at a site near Leipzig.

Another section of the website features the pictures of eight tigers - three which appear to have died in the last nine years. The tigers include 190kg Kiara, 20-year-old Aschanti, and two-year-old cub Imana.

Social media posts appearing to be from the trainer show several pictures of the tigers playing in the enclosures.

It also says the tigers are looked after and kept healthy in an animal-friendly environment.
body.zh: 一只被认为属于德国“虎女王”的逃跑老虎在袭击其饲养员后被警方击毙。 警方告诉 BBC，周日，一名 72 岁的男子在德国莱比锡市郊区一处私人设施内的动物围栏内遭到袭击，身受重伤。 老虎逃离了围栏，不久后被武装警察发现，并开枪打死了它。 据信，该围场的所有者是颇受争议的驯兽师兼私人业主卡门·赞德(Carmen Zander)，她自称是德国的“老虎女王”。 据当地媒体报道，这只动物是德国施科伊迪茨镇附近工业园区饲养的八只大型猫科动物之一。 警方在给英国广播公司的一份声明中表示，警方射杀了这只雄性老虎，以消除公众面临的任何进一步风险。 它补充说，当地警察局于周日当地时间12点50分（英国夏令时11点50分）左右接到紧急电话，警员迅速赶到现场。 没有其他动物逃离该地点，警方已计划使用无人机进行搜索，以确保该地点完全安全。 区长托马斯·德鲁斯卡特（Thomas Druskat）呼吁重新安置其他动物，并告诉当地媒体，如果其他人受到伤害，会发生什么是“不可想象的”。 附近居民告诉德新社（DPA），这一事件“可怕且令人担忧”，其中一人声称这些动物没有得到适当的饲养条件。 动物权利慈善机构善待动物组织呼吁政府采取行动，并告诉 DPA 需要制定更严格的规则来保护私人拥有的动物。 据一家使用詹德名字和昵称的网站称，这位驯兽师向公众举办“令人难忘”且“独一无二”的老虎抚摸活动。 该网站称，游客可以在莱比锡附近的一个地点付费抚摸“250公斤重的猛兽”。 该网站的另一部分展示了八只老虎的照片，其中三只似乎在过去九年里已经死亡。这些老虎包括 190 公斤重的 Kiara、20 岁的 Aschanti 和两岁的幼崽 Imana。 似乎来自驯兽师的社交媒体帖子显示了几张老虎在围栏里玩耍的照片。 它还说，老虎在对动物友好的环境中得到照顾并保持健康。

reflection.en: This incident reminds us of the inherent power of wild creatures and the serious responsibility that comes with managing them. Proverbs 27:12 encourages us to foresee danger and take precautions, highlighting the wisdom in careful stewardship to prevent harm. When foresight is lacking, the consequences can be severe for both humans and animals.

title.en: What is Ebola and what makes the latest outbreak so concerning?
title.zh: 埃博拉是什么？最新疫情为何如此令人担忧？

summary.en: The WHO has declared an international health emergency in multiple African countries over the spread of the deadly disease.
summary.zh: 世界卫生组织已宣布，由于这种致命疾病的传播，多个非洲国家进入国际卫生紧急状态。

body.en:
There have been more than 80 reported deaths from an outbreak of Ebola, which has been declared a public health emergency in central sub-Saharan Africa. 

On Sunday, the World Health Organization (WHO) announced that the surge in cases is of "international concern" but has emphasised that it does not meet pandemic criteria .

The director-general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, Jean Kaseya, has said that he is in "panic mode" over the outbreak.

"Currently, I am on panic mode because people are dying. I don't have medicines, I don't have vaccines to support countries," he said.

Kaseya has called on Western nations to support the local research and production of medicines and vaccines for diseases like Ebola in Africa, warning the health emergency has the potential to spread.

"This is the equity issue. Western countries, they don't understand that, when Africa is affected, they are also at risk, because people are flying every day," he said.

The disease is classified as a zoonotic viral hemorrhagic fever, which can be passed between humans and other primates.

Symptoms are typically flu-like to begin with — making it hard to distinguish from other illnesses — before progressing to severe fevers and muscle pain, internal and external bleeding, and multi-organ failure.

The disease can be spread via direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person, making medical staff treating Ebola patients the most at risk of catching the disease.

It was first reported among humans in 1976 and has since caused intermittent outbreaks in central and West Africa.

The largest of these was the 2014 Western African epidemic, which killed an estimated 11,325 people, mainly in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

Ebola has six viral strains, four of which are significant to humans, but only one of which has approved vaccines and treatments.

The WHO has said that the current outbreak is being driven by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are currently no approved medical preventatives or specific medications.

However, the Bundibugyo strain is considered less lethal than the Zaire and Sudan strains that have sparked previous outbreaks.

While those viruses have fatality rates of 80 to 90 per cent and 50 per cent respectively, Bundibugyo is thought to kill around 40 per cent of those that it infects.

That said, the virus has been spreading for weeks in a part of the world where civil war and distrust of government interventions make public health policy difficult to implement.

The first known case of this outbreak was a nurse who developed symptoms on 24 April, nearly a month before the WHO confirmed an outbreak.

title.en: Ukrainian drone strikes kill four in Russia in its biggest attack in over a year
title.zh: 乌克兰无人机袭击俄罗斯，造成四人死亡，这是一年多来最大规模的袭击

summary.en: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine's increased attacks on Moscow have produced a "change in the balance of actions at the front".
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At least four ‌people have been killed, including three in the Moscow region, after Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on the Russian capital in more than a year.

A fourth person was killed in the Belgorod region bordering northeastern Ukraine, local authorities said on Sunday (local time), while Russia's defence ministry said that ‌by midday more than 1,000 Ukrainian drones had been downed over the country in the past 24 hours.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had vowed retribution on Friday following Russia's heaviest drone and missile attack on Kyiv over a two-day period since the war started more than four years ago.

Confirming the attack, Zelenskyy posted a video on X of a drone in flight, columns of black smoke and fire crews trying to extinguish flames.

"Our responses to Russia's ‌prolongation of the ‌war and its attacks ⁠on our cities and communities are entirely justified," he said.

He added that Ukraine was able to strike targets more than 500km from the border despite dense Russian air defences around Moscow.

Speaking later in his nightly video address, Zelenskyy said Ukraine's increased military activity had produced a "change in the balance of actions at the front, which is now tangible".

"For instance, the activity indicators for today are such that our active measures are greater than those of Russia. This is ⁠a very substantial result," he said, without elaborating.

"To the sound of Eurovision songs, the Kyiv regime, financed by the EU, carried out yet another mass terrorist attack," TASS news agency cited the ministry's spokeswoman Maria Zakharova as saying.

Ukraine has stepped up drone attacks on targets deep inside Russia in recent weeks, aiming to knock out oil refineries, depots and pipelines, as both sides seek to degrade each other's infrastructure.

TASS cited Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin ‌as saying air defences had destroyed 81 drones headed for Moscow since midnight, the largest attack on the capital in more than a year.

Sobyanin said 12 people were wounded, mostly near the entrance to Moscow's oil refinery, while three houses were damaged. The "technology" of the refinery was not damaged, he said.

Moscow regional governor Andrei Vorobyov said a woman was killed when a home was hit in Khimki, north of the capital, adding that rescuers were searching the debris for another person. Two men were killed in the village of Pogorelki in the Mytishchi district.

One of the victims was an Indian citizen working in Russia, the Indian embassy in Moscow said in a statement.

Several residential high-rises and infrastructure facilities were damaged, he said.

title.en: UAE reports drone strike at nuclear power plant as Trump says 'clock is ticking' for Iran
title.zh: 阿联酋报告核电站遭无人机袭击，特朗普称伊朗“时日无多”

summary.en: Officials report that a drone strike has targeted the United Arab Emirates' only nuclear power plant, causing a fire.

body.en:
A drone strike caused a fire at a nuclear power plant in the United Arab Emirates, officials there said overnight, as United States President Donald Trump said Iran must act "fast" after efforts to end the US-Israeli war with Iran appeared to have stalled.

Emirati officials said they were investigating the source of the strike and that the UAE had the full right to respond to such "terrorist attacks".

The UAE defence ministry said two other drones had been "successfully" dealt with, and that the drones had been launched from the "western border". It did not elaborate.

The drone that got through hit an electrical generator outside the inner perimeter of the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant, the Abu Dhabi media office said. Radiological safety levels were unaffected, and there were no injuries, it said.

The International Atomic Energy Agency said emergency diesel generators were providing power to the plant's "unit 3", and called for "maximum military restraint" near any nuclear power plant, adding that it was following the situation closely.

During the war that began with US and Israeli strikes against Iran on 28 February, Iran has repeatedly targeted the UAE and other Gulf states that host US military bases.

Iran stepped up such attacks on the UAE earlier this month after Trump announced a naval mission to try to open the Strait of Hormuz, which Trump retreated from after 48 hours.

More than five weeks after a tenuous ceasefire in the conflict took effect, US and Iranian demands remain far apart despite diplomatic efforts to end the war and reopen the strait, the world's most important shipping route for oil and gas.

The US has called for Iran to dismantle its nuclear program and lift its hold on the Strait. Iran has demanded compensation for war damage, an end to a US blockade of Iranian ports and a halt to fighting on all fronts, including in Lebanon, where Israel is carrying out a bombing campaign and ground invasion.

Trump, whose harsh rhetoric has failed to break the stalemate, said in a post on Truth Social: "For Iran, the Clock is Ticking, and they better get moving, FAST, or there won’t be anything left of them. TIME IS OF THE ESSENCE!"

Trump is expected to meet top national security advisers on Tuesday (local time) to discuss options for military action regarding Iran, Axios reported.

Trump held talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week without securing an indication from China that it would help resolve the conflict and has previously threatened to resume attacks if Iran does not agree to a deal.

title.en: Young Czechs drink less beer but risk other addictions
title.zh: 捷克年轻人喝啤酒较少，但面临其他成瘾风险

summary.en: The Czech Republic, the beer world champion, has seen a record decline in consumption. Younger generations are drinking less. Breweries are worried, but health experts say it's good news.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Czech Republic, the beer world champion, has seen a record decline in consumption. Younger generations are drinking less. Breweries are worried, but health experts say it's good news.

The Czech Republic, which boasts a population of 10 million, is a famously beer-loving nation. Nobody in the world drinks as much beer as the Czechs do — for decades, they have nabbed the top spot for most per capita beer consumption lists, only occasionally ranking second. Traditionally, the pub has formed the heart of a Czech community, being a place for people to meet, play cards, and discuss life, politics and literature. Beer, pubs and lively conversation have also been depicted in the works of the Czech writers Jaroslav Hasek, Bohumil Hrabal and Jaroslav Rudis.

For centuries, beer has played a role in what is now known as the Czech Republic. Even during times of economic decline when the country, then known as Czechoslovakia, was under communist rule, Czech beer, particularly Pilsner, continued to be exported to large parts of the world. Today, several cases of Pilsner Urquell that have been blessed are sent to the Vatican each Easter. Whether any of the popes actually drink the beer is uncertain.

Pilsner's competitor Budvar, which is based in the city of Ceske Budejovice and is best known for the original Budweiser, is one of the few companies in the country that withstood the pressure to privatize after the fall of communism and remains state-owned to this day.

News about beer prices, consumption, production, sales and exports is still followed with great interest in the Czech Republic. The recent announcement by the Czech Beer and Malt Association that beer consumption in the Czech Republic had fallen to a historic low of 121 liters per capita in 2025 even overshadowed reports of rising diesel and gasoline prices in conjunction with Israel and the US' war with Iran .

"Every Czech drank eight fewer large beers last year than in 2024," noted the public broadcaster Cesky rozhlas, which gave a great deal of attention to the subject alongside other media outlets.

"In recent years, Czechs have been placing greater emphasis on moderate consumption and leading healthier lifestyles," explained Tomas Slunecko, head of the Czech Beer and Malt Association. "And when they do go out for a beer, they are more interested in the variety of options available and in quality rather than quantity. This is also reflected in the long-term rise in interest in non-alcoholic beers." Furthermore, people are increasingly drinking beer outside of pubs and restaurants, according to the association.

body.zh: 啤酒世界冠军捷克共和国的消费量出现了创纪录的下降。年轻一代的饮酒量越来越少。啤酒厂很担心，但健康专家表示这是个好消息。 拥有1000万人口的捷克共和国是出了名的热爱啤酒的国家。世界上没有人像捷克人喝那么多啤酒——几十年来，他们在大多数人均啤酒消费排行榜上名列前茅，只是偶尔排名第二。传统上，酒吧是捷克社区的中心，是人们聚会、打牌、讨论生活、政治和文学的地方。捷克作家雅罗斯拉夫·哈塞克（Jaroslav Hasek）、博胡米尔·赫拉巴尔（Bohumil Hrabal）和雅罗斯拉夫·鲁迪斯（Jaroslav Rudis）的作品中也描绘了啤酒、酒吧和热闹的谈话。 几个世纪以来，啤酒在现在的捷克共和国发挥着重要作用。即使在经济衰退时期，当时的捷克斯洛伐克处于共产主义统治之下，捷克啤酒，尤其是比尔森啤酒，仍然继续出口到世界大部分地区。如今，每年复活节都会有几箱经过祝福的比尔森啤酒被送往梵蒂冈。是否有教皇真正喝过这种啤酒还不确定。 比尔森啤酒的竞争对手 Budvar 总部位于捷克布提约维采市，以原版百威啤酒而闻名，是该国少数几家在共产主义垮台后顶住私有化压力并至今仍为国有的公司之一。 有关啤酒价格、消费、生产、销售和出口的新闻仍然受到捷克共和国的极大关注。捷克啤酒和麦芽协会最近宣布，捷克共和国的啤酒消费量将在 2025 年降至人均 121 升的历史低点，甚至掩盖了因以色列和美国与伊朗战争而导致柴油和汽油价格上涨的报道。 公共广播公司 Cesky rozhlas 指出：“去年每个捷克人喝的大杯啤酒比 2024 年少了 8 杯。”该广播公司与其他媒体一起对这一主题给予了极大的关注。 “近年来，捷克人更加重视适度消费和更健康的生活方式，”捷克啤酒和麦芽协会负责人托马斯·斯鲁内科 (Tomas Slunecko) 解释道。 “当他们出去喝啤酒时，他们对各种选择以及质量而不是数量更感兴趣。这也反映在对无酒精啤酒兴趣的长期增长上。”此外，据该协会称，人们越来越多地在酒吧和餐馆外喝啤酒。 去年，捷克共和国销售的啤酒中只有约四分之一是在酒吧和餐馆消费的。随后，该协会呼吁政府...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to compassion for vulnerable people. Galatians 6:2 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with practical compassion and welcome, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到对脆弱群体的怜悯。Galatians 6:2提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以具体的怜悯与接纳来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: North Korean women's football team makes rare visit to South
title.zh: 朝鲜女足队罕见访问韩国

summary.en: A North Korean women's football club has become the country's first group of athletes in eight years to visit the South.
summary.zh: 朝鲜女子足球队八年来首次访问韩国，成为该国首批访问韩国的运动员团体。

body.en:
A North Korean women's football club has become the country's first group of athletes in eight years to visit the South.

A women's football team from the isolated communist country of North Korea  arrived in South Korea on Sunday, a rare visit that has generated strong public interest.

The visit by the club Naegohyang Women's FC is the first by athletes from the North to the South in eight years. It was approved under the inter-Korean exchange law despite the current strained ties between the two neighbors.

The team, which is to play in the Asian Champions League semifinals, arrived at South Korea's Incheon International Airport on a plane from China.

All 7,087 tickets made available to the general public for Wednesday's match ​against South Korea's Suwon FC Women in Suwon sold out within a day.

The winner will face either Melbourne City or Tokyo Verdy in the final in Suwon on Saturday, with the North Korean team expected to return home the following day if eliminated, though its visit is approved through the weekend.

Seoul's Unification Ministry said it has earmarked 300 million won (€172,000; $200,000) from an inter-Korean cooperation fund ⁠to finance ​a cheering squad for both sides.

It has stressed that the event is a way ​to promote mutual understanding between the two Koreas, which have been separated since the 1950-1953 Korean War.

The communist North, under its authoritarian leader Kim Jong Un , has in recent years called the South the "most hostile state" and said it opposes reunification. 

This contrasts with the approach of South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, who has called for improved ties.

In another sign of the South's desire for rapprochement, Unification Minister Chung Dong-young is also considering attending the match, according ⁠to South Korean media.

However, in line with Asian Football Confederation rules, the Korean Unification flag, often seen at international ⁠sports fixtures involving both sides, will not be used at the match as it involves clubs and not national teams.
body.zh: 朝鲜女子足球俱乐部成为该国八年来第一批访问韩国的运动员。 来自孤立的共产主义国家朝鲜的一支女子足球队于周日抵达韩国，这是一次罕见的访问，引起了公众的强烈兴趣。 内乡乡女子足球俱乐部此次来访是八年来朝鲜运动员首次来到韩国。尽管目前两个邻国之间的关系紧张，但该协议还是根据朝韩交换法获得批准。 参加亚冠半决赛的球队从中国乘坐飞机抵达韩国仁川国际机场。 周三在水原对阵韩国水原女足的比赛的全部 7,087 张门票在一天之内就售罄。 获胜者将在周六于水原举行的决赛中对阵墨尔本城队或东京绿茵队，朝鲜队如果被淘汰，预计将在第二天回国，尽管其访问已在周末获得批准。 首尔统一部表示，已从朝韩合作基金中拨出 3 亿韩元（172,000 欧元；200,000 美元），用于资助双方啦啦队。 它强调，该活动是促进自 1950-1953 年朝鲜战争以来分裂的两个朝鲜之间相互了解的一种方式。 近年来，在独裁领导人金正恩领导下的共产主义朝鲜称韩国为“最敌对的国家”，并表示反对统一。 这与韩国总统李在明呼吁改善关系的做法形成鲜明对比。 据韩国媒体报道，韩国统一部长官郑东泳也在考虑参加比赛，这是韩国渴望和解的另一个迹象。 然而，根据亚洲足球联合会的规定，在双方参与的国际体育赛事中经常看到的韩国统一旗帜将不会在比赛中使用，因为涉及的是俱乐部而不是国家队。

reflection.en: This rare visit by athletes across a long-standing divide offers a glimpse of connection where hostility has prevailed. It reminds us that even small acts of engagement can begin to dismantle barriers that separate people, echoing the hope for walls of hostility to come down.
reflection.zh: 这次运动员跨越长期分歧的罕见访问，为长期敌对的双方提供了一线连接的希望。它提醒我们，即使是微小的接触行动，也能开始拆除隔绝人们的障碍，呼应了拆除敌意之墙的盼望。

verse.textEn: For he himself is our peace, who has made the two groups one and has destroyed the barrier, the dividing wall of hostility.
verse.textZh: 因他使我们和睦，将两下合而为一，拆毁了中间隔断的墙。

title.en: EV battery supply chains in focus as China halts sulphuric acid exports
title.zh: 中国暂停硫酸出口，电动汽车电池供应链受关注

summary.en: China's decision to stop exporting sulphuric acid is expected to create pressure on global supply chains for both electric vehicle batteries and fertilizers.
summary.zh: 中国停止出口硫酸预计将对电动汽车电池和化肥的全球供应链造成压力。

body.en:
China has banned exports of sulphuric acid, the world's most used industrial chemical and a crucial ingredient in battery and clothing manufacturing, as well as fertiliser production and metal processing industries.

The move comes amid pressures on supply of the chemical after conflict in the Middle East disrupted sulphur shipments through the Strait of Hormuz earlier this year.

Marina Zhang from the University of Technology Sydney's Australia-China Relations Institute said that, while the ban may have been presented by China as temporary, it signals a policy shift from Australia's largest trading partner towards increasingly prioritising control over industrial inputs.

"It's not just finished products, but the upstream materials, processing technologies and basic industrial ingredients that allow advanced manufacturing to scale … So while the immediate measure may be temporary, the underlying logic is structural," Zhang told SBS News.

Sulphur is the primary ingredient used to produce sulphuric acid, meaning shipping and processing delays of the raw material in the Gulf region have created flow-on effects for manufacturers reliant on a steady supply.

In 2025, about half of the global seaborne supply of sulphur came from the Middle East.

China accounted for a significant share of sulphuric acid shipments from Asia last year and remains one of the world's largest exporters. The loss of that supply is now raising concerns among overseas buyers already scrambling to secure alternative sources.

While the impacts are expected to be spread across multiple industries, analysts say battery supply chains could be among the most exposed.

Zhang said the situation "reveals a paradox at the heart of the clean-energy transition … which depends on minerals that require very energy-intensive, chemical-intensive and often environmentally difficult processing".

"Yet many Western countries have spent decades outsourcing precisely those 'dirty' industrial activities."

Sulphuric acid also plays an important role in processing metals such as nickel and copper, both used extensively in electric vehicle batteries and energy storage systems.

Indonesia's rapidly expanding nickel-processing industry is considered particularly vulnerable to the bans.

The country has become a major producer of battery-grade nickel used in global electric vehicle (EV) supply chains, including by manufacturers linked to Chinese battery maker CATL.

Refining lower-grade nickel ores into battery materials requires large volumes of sulphuric acid for a process known as high-pressure acid leaching.

If supplies remain constrained, refiners could face higher production costs, delays and increased competition for feedstock, potentially flowing through to battery makers and EV...
body.zh: 中国已禁止出口硫酸，硫酸是世界上使用最广泛的工业化学品，也是电池和服装制造、化肥生产和金属加工业的关键成分。 今年早些时候，中东冲突扰乱了通过霍尔木兹海峡的硫磺运输，导致化学品供应面临压力。 悉尼科技大学澳中关系研究所的玛丽娜·张表示，虽然中国提出的禁令可能是暂时的，但它标志着澳大利亚最大贸易伙伴的政策转变，越来越优先考虑对工业投入的控制。 “这不仅仅是成品，还有上游材料、加工技术和基本工业原料，使先进制造业能够规模化……因此，虽然眼前的措施可能是暂时的，但潜在的逻辑是结构性的，”张告诉SBS新闻。 硫是用于生产硫酸的主要成分，这意味着海湾地区原材料的运输和加工延迟对依赖稳定供应的制造商产生了连锁效应。 到 2025 年，全球海运硫磺供应量的一半左右来自中东。 去年，中国占亚洲硫酸出口量的很大一部分，并且仍然是世界最大的出口国之一。这种供应的损失现在引起了已经在争相寻找替代来源的海外买家的担忧。 虽然预计影响将波及多个行业，但分析师表示，电池供应链可能是受影响最大的行业之一。 张说，这种情况“揭示了清洁能源转型核心的一个悖论……这取决于需要能源密集型、化学密集型且通常对环境困难的加工的矿物”。 “然而，许多西方国家花费了数十年的时间，将那些‘肮脏’的工业活动外包出去。” 硫酸在镍和铜等金属加工中也发挥着重要作用，这两种金属广泛用于电动汽车电池和储能系统。 印度尼西亚快速扩张的镍加工业被认为特别容易受到禁令的影响。 中国已成为全球电动汽车（EV）供应链中使用的电池级镍的主要生产国，其中包括与中国电池制造商宁德时代相关的制造商。 将低品位镍矿石精炼成电池材料需要大量硫酸，这一过程被称为高压酸浸出。 如果供应仍然受到限制，炼油厂可能面临更高的生产成本、延误和原料竞争加剧，并可能流向电池制造商和电动汽车……

reflection.en: The halt in sulphuric acid exports highlights the interconnectedness of global supply chains and the importance of foresight. When nations or industries rely heavily on single sources, prudence is needed to anticipate potential disruptions and prepare for their impact.
reflection.zh: 硫酸出口的暂停凸显了全球供应链的相互关联性以及预见性的重要。当国家或行业严重依赖单一来源时，需要审慎地预见潜在的干扰并为其影响做好准备。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: Venezuela deports Maduro ally Alex Saab to US
title.zh: 委内瑞拉将马杜罗盟友亚历克斯·萨博驱逐至美国

summary.en: Alex Saab, a former ally of Venezuela's ex-leader Maduro, has been deported to the US. His deportation follows the ouster and capture of Maduro by US forces in January, leading to Saab falling out of favor with the new administration.
summary.zh: 委内瑞拉已将前领导人马杜罗的盟友亚历克斯·萨博驱逐至美国。自马杜罗于一月被美国军队推翻并抓捕后，萨博便在新政府中失宠。

body.en:
Alex Saab fell out of favor with the new administration that took power since Maduro’s ouster and capture by US forces in January.

Venezuela's government said Saturday it had deported former Industry Minister Alex Saab to the United States.  

"The deportation measure was adopted in consideration of the fact that the aforementioned Colombian citizen is involved in the commission of various crimes in the United States of America, as is public, well-known and reported," the Venezuelan immigration administration said in a statement.

In this case, the country's immigration authority determined that Saab was a Colombian national and ordered him "deported" to the United States.

The Colombia-born Saab managed a vast import network for Maduro's administration and built a fortune through government contracts.

He has been accused of acting as a frontman and money launderer for Maduro and his government. Maduro, in exchange, granted him Venezuelan citizenship and a diplomatic passport.

Saab was first arrested in Cape Verde in 2020 over allegations of money laundering and corruption. He was extradited to the United States the following year.

The 54-year-old and his business partner Alvaro Pulido were charged with running a network that exploited a subsidized food aid program for Venezuela known as CLAP.

The men were ultimately accused of laundering $350 million (€301 million) out of Venezuela.

A US judge later dismissed most charges against Saab. But he still faced one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering, which carried a 20-year jail term.

However, in December 2023, Saab was released from US custody as part of a prisoner exchange deal with Venezuela.

But Saab fell out of favor with the new administration that took power since Maduro's ouster and capture by the US military in January.

Interim President Rodriguez, Maduro's former vice president, has fired Saab from the Cabinet and stripped him of all his posts.

His wife Camilla Fabri, who served as deputy minister for international communication, was also dismissed in February.

Saab's extradition to the US could deepen divisions inside Rodríguez's fragile ruling coalition in Caracas.
body.zh: 自从一月份马杜罗被美军赶下台并被俘后，亚历克斯·萨博就失去了上台新政府的青睐。 委内瑞拉政府周六表示，已将前工业部长亚历克斯·萨博驱逐到美国。 委内瑞拉移民管理局在一份声明中表示：“考虑到上述哥伦比亚公民在美国参与了各种众所周知的犯罪行为，因此采取驱逐措施。” 在这种情况下，该国移民当局认定萨博是哥伦比亚国民，并下令将他“驱逐”到美国。 出生于哥伦比亚的萨博为马杜罗政府管理着庞大的进口网络，并通过政府合同积累了巨额财富。 他被指控充当马杜罗及其政府的领军人物和洗钱者。作为交换，马杜罗授予他委内瑞拉公民身份和外交护照。 萨博于 2020 年首次在佛得角因洗钱和腐败指控被捕。次年他被引渡到美国。 54 岁的他和他的商业伙伴阿尔瓦罗·普利多 (Alvaro Pulido) 被指控运营一个网络，利用委内瑞拉一项名为 CLAP 的粮食援助补贴计划。 这些人最终被指控从委内瑞拉洗钱 3.5 亿美元（3.01 亿欧元）。 一名美国法官后来驳回了对萨博的大部分指控。但他仍然面临一项共谋洗钱罪名，被判处 20 年监禁。 然而，2023 年 12 月，作为与委内瑞拉的囚犯交换协议的一部分，萨博被从美国拘留中释放。 但自从一月份马杜罗被美军赶下台并被俘后，萨博就失去了上台新政府的青睐。 马杜罗的前副总统、临时总统罗德里格斯已将萨博从内阁中解雇，并剥夺了他的所有职位。 他的妻子卡米拉·法布里（Camilla Fabri）担任国际通讯部副部长，也在二月份被解雇。 萨博被引渡到美国可能会加深罗德里格斯在加拉加斯脆弱的执政联盟内部的分歧。

reflection.en: The dramatic shift in Alex Saab's fortunes, from ally to deportee, highlights the transient nature of human power and political alliances. This reminds us that while human leaders rise and fall, it is 雅伟 who ultimately determines the course of nations and individuals.
reflection.zh: 亚历克斯·萨博从盟友到被驱逐的命运巨变，凸显了人类权力和政治联盟的短暂性。这提醒我们，尽管人类领袖有兴有衰，但最终决定国家和个人命运的，是雅伟。

verse.textEn: It is God who judges: He brings one down, he exalts another.
verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

title.en: Germany stakes claim in new space race
title.zh: 德国在新太空竞赛中占据一席之地

summary.en: German companies are actively developing satellites and space applications to participate in the growing and profitable space industry, which serves both civilian and military needs.
summary.zh: 德国各地的公司正在开发卫星和空间应用，以参与利润丰厚的航天工业，该行业对民用和军事目的都日益重要。

body.en:
German companies of all sizes and all over the country are developing satellites and space applications. They want to be part of the lucrative industry, which is increasingly crucial for civilian and military purposes.

The space industry is a multibillion-dollar business. According to a study by the German consulting firm Roland Berger and the Federation of German Industries (BDI), the market is worth around $600 billion (€516 billion) and growing. By 2040, it is predicted to be worth $2.32 trillion. That is about four times Germany's federal budget in 2025.

And many want a slice of the new  private spaceflight  pie. Currently, some $150 billion is flowing into the "upstream market," which "comprises production of the infrastructure required on Earth and in space, from launch pads, ground segments, and satellites," according to Roland Berger. A much larger share — approximately $450 billion — has been invested into downstream applications, which "consists of space-based solutions — positioning, navigation & timing, Earth observation, and satellite communications."

"NewSpace is essentially a data business," said Matthias Wachter, the managing director of the BDI's NewSpace Initiative and co-director of its Innovation, Security and Technology division.

Space travel has changed dramatically since its early days. During the Cold War , it was primarily a race between the United States and the Soviet Union , with the impetus and funding coming from the state.

But in about 2000, governments began to slip into the role of clients. Since then, private companies have been providing rocket launch services and developing satellites. Major players SpaceX and Blue Origin were also born at the turn of the century.

Reusable launch vehicles have also made space travel significantly more affordable, opening up new business opportunities and paving the way for various applications. According to the US consulting firm McKinsey, launch costs alone have fallen by 90% over the past 20 years. 

While SpaceX and Blue Origin have captured the public imagination, there are many other companies in the space business, including in Germany, particularly as space technology is so versatile.

body.zh: 财政部长命令与中国有联系的公司剥离北方矿业公司以保护澳大利亚的利益。 澳大利亚命令与中国有关的股东出售其在正在开发稀土矿的北方矿业公司的股份。 财务主管吉姆·查尔默斯 (Jim Chalmers) 表示，由于担心中国投资者试图控制北方矿产公司，他已于周一发布了命令。 这家总部位于澳大利亚的矿业公司正在西澳大利亚州最北部开发布朗斯山脉项目，以开采大量的镝和铽储量。 查尔默在一份声明中表示，他的决定旨在保护该国的国家利益并确保遵守其外国投资框架。 他说：“我们运营着一个强大且非歧视性的外国投资框架，如果需要，我们将采取进一步行动，以保护我们与此事相关的国家利益。” 镝和铽是对于耐热高性能磁体至关重要的重稀土元素。这些产品用于清洁能源应用，例如混合动力汽车和风力涡轮机，以及专业国防应用。 它开采约 60% 的原材料，并精炼约占全球供应量的 95%-98%。这使其几乎垄断了加工商业镝。 北方矿业公司的稀土预计将在澳大利亚新建的炼油厂进行加工。 当这两个项目上线时，澳大利亚将成为第一个重要的非中国加工镝来源国。 包括澳大利亚和美国在内的西方国家正在寻求限制中国对关键矿产的投资。 近年来，中国投资者一直寻求在北方矿业公司持有大量股份。 关于查尔默最近的处置令，六名股东中有三名的地址在中国，两名在香港，一名在英属维尔京群岛上市。 但澳大利亚早在 2024 年就已经使用外国收购法，迫使五名投资者出售其在北方矿业公司的股份。 2025 年，财政部采取了史无前例的举措，将最大股东之一告上法庭，称其藐视出售令，而是将股份转入其自己董事的名下。

body.en:
Taiwan will not provoke any conflict but will also not give up its sovereignty, said its president Lai Ching-te after a high-stakes summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping where they discussed the issue of Taiwan's independence.

According to Chinese state media, Xi had told Trump that Taiwan, a self-governed island claimed by Beijing, was "the most important issue" in bilateral ties and mishandling it could lead to conflict.

After his visit to Beijing, Trump issued a warning to Taiwan , telling Fox News: "I'm not looking to have somebody go independent."

The US is a longstanding ally of Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the island with the means to defend itself.

During his interview, Trump said that US policy on Taiwan had not changed, while making it clear he did not seek conflict with Beijing.

Trump also told reporters Xi had felt "very strongly" about Taiwan but Trump had "made no commitment either way".

Under Lai and his predecessor Tsai Ing-wen, the Taiwanese government has for years maintained that there is no need to formally declare independence because it already considers Taiwan as a sovereign nation.

Lai reiterated this stance in his Facebook post, which was his first direct response to the summit, saying "there is no 'Taiwan independence' issue".

"Taiwan, the Republic of China, is a sovereign and independent democratic country," he wrote, adding that "Taiwan's future must follow the will of all the Taiwanese people."

Most people in Taiwan consider themselves a sovereign nation. But many also favour keeping the "status quo" in cross-strait relations: neither unifying with China nor formally declaring independence.

Beijing has been vocal in its dislike of Lai, who it has described as a "troublemaker" and "destroyer of cross-strait peace".

Lai wrote on Facebook that "Taiwan will not provoke, will not escalate conflict, but will not under pressure give up national sovereignty and dignity, as well as the democratic and free way of life".

"Taiwan has always been a firm defender of the status quo on both sides of the Strait, not a party to change it," he wrote.

He also said that that Taiwan was willing to "promote healthy and orderly exchanges and dialogue with China on the premise of equality and dignity", but it rejects China's attempt at using "unification" as a cover to coerce Taiwan into dialogue.

Earlier, the presidential spokesperson had said it was "self-evident" that Taiwan was "a sovereign, independent democratic country", while adding that they were committed to maintaining the status quo.

Beijing has emphasised it wants "peaceful reunification" with Taiwan, but it has not ruled out the use of force to take the island.

title.en: EV battery supply chains in focus as China halts sulphuric acid exports
title.zh: 中国暂停硫酸出口，电动汽车电池供应链受关注

summary.en: China's decision to stop exporting sulphuric acid is expected to create pressure on global supply chains for both electric vehicle batteries and fertilizers.
summary.zh: 中国停止出口硫酸预计将对电动汽车电池和化肥的全球供应链造成压力。

body.en:
China has banned exports of sulphuric acid, the world's most used industrial chemical and a crucial ingredient in battery and clothing manufacturing, as well as fertiliser production and metal processing industries.

The move comes amid pressures on supply of the chemical after conflict in the Middle East disrupted sulphur shipments through the Strait of Hormuz earlier this year.

Marina Zhang from the University of Technology Sydney's Australia-China Relations Institute said that, while the ban may have been presented by China as temporary, it signals a policy shift from Australia's largest trading partner towards increasingly prioritising control over industrial inputs.

"It's not just finished products, but the upstream materials, processing technologies and basic industrial ingredients that allow advanced manufacturing to scale … So while the immediate measure may be temporary, the underlying logic is structural," Zhang told SBS News.

Sulphur is the primary ingredient used to produce sulphuric acid, meaning shipping and processing delays of the raw material in the Gulf region have created flow-on effects for manufacturers reliant on a steady supply.

In 2025, about half of the global seaborne supply of sulphur came from the Middle East.

China accounted for a significant share of sulphuric acid shipments from Asia last year and remains one of the world's largest exporters. The loss of that supply is now raising concerns among overseas buyers already scrambling to secure alternative sources.

While the impacts are expected to be spread across multiple industries, analysts say battery supply chains could be among the most exposed.

Zhang said the situation "reveals a paradox at the heart of the clean-energy transition … which depends on minerals that require very energy-intensive, chemical-intensive and often environmentally difficult processing".

"Yet many Western countries have spent decades outsourcing precisely those 'dirty' industrial activities."

Sulphuric acid also plays an important role in processing metals such as nickel and copper, both used extensively in electric vehicle batteries and energy storage systems.

Indonesia's rapidly expanding nickel-processing industry is considered particularly vulnerable to the bans.

The country has become a major producer of battery-grade nickel used in global electric vehicle (EV) supply chains, including by manufacturers linked to Chinese battery maker CATL.

Refining lower-grade nickel ores into battery materials requires large volumes of sulphuric acid for a process known as high-pressure acid leaching.

body.zh: 中国已禁止出口硫酸，硫酸是世界上使用最广泛的工业化学品，也是电池和服装制造、化肥生产和金属加工业的关键成分。 今年早些时候，中东冲突扰乱了通过霍尔木兹海峡的硫磺运输，导致化学品供应面临压力。 悉尼科技大学澳中关系研究所的玛丽娜·张表示，虽然中国提出的禁令可能是暂时的，但它标志着澳大利亚最大贸易伙伴的政策转变，越来越优先考虑对工业投入的控制。 “这不仅仅是成品，还有上游材料、加工技术和基本工业原料，使先进制造业能够规模化……因此，虽然眼前的措施可能是暂时的，但潜在的逻辑是结构性的，”张告诉SBS新闻。 硫是用于生产硫酸的主要成分，这意味着海湾地区原材料的运输和加工延迟对依赖稳定供应的制造商产生了连锁效应。 到 2025 年，全球海运硫磺供应量的一半左右来自中东。 去年，中国占亚洲硫酸出口量的很大一部分，并且仍然是世界最大的出口国之一。这种供应的损失现在引起了已经在争相寻找替代来源的海外买家的担忧。 虽然预计影响将波及多个行业，但分析师表示，电池供应链可能是受影响最大的行业之一。 张说，这种情况“揭示了清洁能源转型核心的一个悖论……这取决于需要能源密集型、化学密集型且通常对环境困难的加工的矿物”。 “然而，许多西方国家花费了数十年的时间，将那些‘肮脏’的工业活动外包出去。” 硫酸在镍和铜等金属加工中也发挥着重要作用，这两种金属广泛用于电动汽车电池和储能系统。 印度尼西亚快速扩张的镍加工业被认为特别容易受到禁令的影响。 中国已成为全球电动汽车（EV）供应链中使用的电池级镍的主要生产国，其中包括与中国电池制造商宁德时代相关的制造商。 将低品位镍矿石精炼成电池材料需要大量硫酸，这一过程被称为高压酸浸出。 如果供应仍然受到限制，炼油厂可能面临更高的生产成本、延误和原料竞争加剧，并可能流向电池制造商和电动汽车……

reflection.en: The halt in sulphuric acid exports highlights the interconnectedness of global supply chains and the importance of foresight. When nations or industries rely heavily on single sources, prudence is needed to anticipate potential disruptions and prepare for their impact.
reflection.zh: 硫酸出口的暂停凸显了全球供应链的相互关联性以及预见性的重要。当国家或行业严重依赖单一来源时，需要审慎地预见潜在的干扰并为其影响做好准备。

title.en: Secret police and propaganda: The Chinese agents spying on expats in US
title.zh: 秘密警察与宣传：中国特工在美国监视海外侨民

summary.en: Experts indicate that two espionage cases in the US reveal China's efforts to exert global influence over the past decade, involving secret police and propaganda targeting expatriates.
summary.zh: 专家指出，美国的两起间谍案凸显了过去十年中国在全球范围内施加影响的企图，其中包括秘密警察和针对海外侨民的宣传活动。

body.en:
The glass-paned office building perched above a ramen store in the heart of Manhattan's Chinatown looked inconspicuous on a busy block of Chinese restaurants, grocery stores and apartments.

In 2022, Lu Jianwang, the 64-year-old president of a Chinese community group, set up shop on one of the floors, creating a space where his attorneys said he planned to help expats renew their driver's licences and play ping pong on a table in a conference room.

But it was not long before the Federal Bureau of Investigation raided the space, and accused Lu of taking orders from the Chinese government to establish the first known overseas police station in the US.

This week, he was found guilty of acting as an unauthorised foreign agent for China, just days after a California politician pleaded guilty to similar offences.

Arcadia Mayor Eileen Wang admitted she posted propaganda on a website targeting the Chinese American community at the behest of the Chinese government.

The two convictions came in the same week that President Donald Trump headed to Beijing for a rare meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, where the two steered clear of topics like espionage and focused on trade .

But experts say the two cases in the US highlight the long-arm of the People's Republic of China (PRC), which has ramped up its attempts to peddle influence around the globe over the past decade, both through its strategic use of "soft power" - funding projects and industries overseas - as well as more covert means.

"It's part of the same sort of strategic approach, which is to tamp down on dissent and to shape a clear narrative around the PRC, and to do that in bolder ways, as we're seeing," said Lauryn Williams, a deputy director with the Center for Strategic and International Studies, which has tracked cases of Chinese espionage in the US since 2000.

Lu, who was supported by dozens of community members during his one-week trial in Brooklyn, could face up to 30 years in prison for the charges linked to the illegal police station.

China has been accused of setting up such stations around the world, with at least 100 reported across 53 countries. Just last week, a UK immigration officer was found guilty of working for Chinese intelligence as part of a "shadow policing operation" .

The Chinese government has at times denied that the stations exist or has described them as places where volunteers help their fellow Chinese citizens with administrative services.

"They are not so-called police stations or police service centres at all," China's Ministry of Public Security said in 2023. The BBC has contacted the Chinese Embassy in the US for comment.

A police investigation into "secret Chinese police stations" in London concluded that "no criminal activity" has taken place.

body.zh: 这座玻璃办公楼坐落在曼哈顿唐人街中心的一家拉面店上方，在繁忙的中餐馆、杂货店和公寓街区中显得不起眼。 2022年，64岁的华人社区团体主席卢建旺在其中一层开设了商店，并开辟了一个空间，他的律师称，他计划帮助外国人更新驾驶执照，并在会议室的桌子上打乒乓球。 但没过多久，美国联邦调查局突袭了该场所，并指控卢接受中国政府的命令，在美国建立了第一个已知的海外警察局。 本周，他被判犯有未经授权的中国外国代理人罪，就在几天前，一名加州政客承认了类似的罪行。 阿卡迪亚市市长王艾琳承认，她应中国政府的要求，在一个针对华裔美国人社区的网站上发布了宣传内容。 这两项定罪发生在唐纳德·特朗普总统前往北京与中国国家主席习近平举行罕见会晤的同一周，两人避开了间谍活动等话题，重点讨论了贸易。 但专家表示，美国的这两起案件凸显了中华人民共和国的长臂，过去十年来，中国加大了在全球范围内兜售影响力的力度，既通过战略性运用“软实力”（为海外项目和产业提供资金），也通过更隐蔽的手段。 战略与国际研究中心副主任劳伦·威廉姆斯(Lauryn Williams)表示：“这是同一种战略方针的一部分，即压制异见，围绕中华人民共和国形成清晰的叙述，并以更大胆的方式做到这一点，正如我们所看到的那样。”该中心自2000年以来一直在追踪中国在美国的间谍活动案件。 卢在布鲁克林为期一周的审判期间得到了数十名社区成员的支持，他可能因与非法警察局有关的指控而面临最高 30 年的监禁。 中国被指控在世界各地设立此类站点，据报道在 53 个国家至少有 100 个。就在上周，一名英国移民官员因参与“影子警务行动”而为中国情报部门工作而被判有罪。 中国政府有时否认这些车站的存在，或将其描述为志愿者为中国同胞提供行政服务的地方。 中国公安部2023年表示：“它们根本不是所谓的警察局或警察服务中心。”BBC已联系中国驻美国大使馆请其置评。 警方对伦敦“中国秘密警察局”的调查得出的结论是“没有发生任何犯罪活动”。 鲁...

reflection.en: The news of secret police operations targeting expatriates highlights the chilling effect of unchecked power. Proverbs 28:15 reminds us how oppressive a wicked ruler can be, creating a climate of fear for those under their sway. In such times, we are called to pray for justice and for the protection of the vulnerable.
reflection.zh: 秘密警察针对海外侨民的行动，凸显了不受约束的权力所带来的寒蝉效应。箴言28:15提醒我们，邪恶的统治者如何像咆哮的狮子般压迫人民，为受其影响的人制造恐惧气氛。在这样的时刻，我们被呼召为公义和对弱者的保护祷告。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Pomp, pageantry but precious little to show for Trump’s Beijing excursion
title.zh: 特朗普北京之行：场面隆重，成果寥寥

summary.en: A high-profile visit by the US president to Beijing featured elaborate ceremonies but produced few concrete outcomes, with no swift end to the Iran war, continued uncertainty over Taiwan, and only vague commercial deals.
summary.zh: 美国总统对北京进行了一次备受瞩目的访问，尽管场面隆重，但在结束伊朗战争、台湾问题的不确定性以及商业协议方面，几乎没有取得任何具体成果。

body.en: No swift end to the Iran war, uncertainty over Taiwan and only vague outlines of commercial deals … but the US president did get to bask in the company of Xi Jinping It was historic, to be sure, but not as anyone had predicted . First there was Donald Trump , a self-declared teetotaler, apparently drinking champagne after Xi Jinping assured him that China’s “great rejuvenation” could go hand in hand with “Make America great again”. Then there was a Chinese military band playing a rendition of the US president’s signature campaign song, YMCA. Beneath giant chandeliers, blue and gold balconies and a big orange backdrop with pagoda-style roofs, Thursday’s state banquet in Beijing featured characters whose presence would have been unthinkable here a decade ago: Elon Musk , the eccentric tech billionaire, Pete Hegseth , the Fox News host turned “secretary of war”, and of course Trump himself, a former reality TV star now leading the world’s biggest superpower. body.zh: 伊朗战争没有迅速结束，台湾问题存在不确定性，商业协议也只有模糊的轮廓……但美国总统确实享受到了习近平的陪伴。可以肯定的是，这是历史性的，但并不像任何人预测的那样。首先是自称禁酒的唐纳德·特朗普，在习近平向他保证中国的“伟大复兴”可以与“让美国再次伟大”齐头并进后，他显然正在喝香槟。随后，中国军乐队演奏了美国总统的标志性竞选歌曲《基督教青年会》。在巨大的吊灯、蓝色和金色的阳台以及带有宝塔式屋顶的橙色大背景下，周四在北京举行的国宴上出现的人物在十年前是不可想象的：古怪的科技亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克、福克斯新闻主持人变身“战争部长”皮特·赫格斯，当然还有特朗普本人，他是一位前电视真人秀明星，现在领导着世界上最大的超级大国。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The elaborate diplomatic efforts described in the news, despite their pomp and pageantry, yielded few tangible results. This reminds us that some struggles are not merely against human leaders or policies, but against deeper, unseen forces that complicate peace and progress. In such complex global challenges, true resolution often requires addressing more...
reflection.zh: 新闻中描述的盛大外交努力，尽管场面隆重，却未能带来多少实质性成果。这提醒我们，有些争战不仅仅是针对人类领袖或政策，而是针对更深层、看不见的力量，这些力量使和平与进步变得复杂。在如此复杂的全球挑战中，真正的解决方案往往需要处理的不仅仅是表面上的谈判。

verse.textEn: For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms.
verse.textZh: 因我们并不是与属血气的争战，乃是与那些执政的、掌权的、管辖这幽暗世界的，以及天空属灵气的恶魔争战。

title.en: As Xi sets a new power dynamic, Trump leaves China with little to brag about
title.zh: 习近平确立新权力格局，特朗普对中国无甚可夸耀

summary.en: A recent summit between the leaders of China and the United States, while largely cordial, indicated a potential shift in the balance of power between the two nations.
summary.zh: 在中美两国领导人的一次大致友好的峰会期间，有迹象表明两国之间的权力平衡可能正在发生变化。

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump hailed it as “the biggest summit ever.” In reality, his less than 48 lavish hours in China yielded few results.

Expectations for any real breakthroughs were always low. But what we saw at the high-stakes summit could still shape the US-China relationship for months and years to come.

China had been signalling for weeks that Taiwan would be its top priority at this summit.

The island’s status has always been a point of conflict between the US and Chinese governments; China claims it as a self-governing province that will eventually be brought under its control, while the US has long been its single largest supplier of the weapons needed to prevent that from happening.

But this week, Chinese President Xi Jinping took it one step further; saying explicitly that from now on, the most important factor in the US-China relationship would be how the US deals with Taiwan.

“The Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-US relations,” Xi told Trump, according to the Chinese Foreign Ministry handout. “If it is handled properly, the bilateral relationship will enjoy overall stability. If handled poorly, the two countries will collide or even clash, putting the entire US-China relationship in an extremely dangerous situation.”

When asked for his version of events later in the day, Trump opted to say nothing. His silence was seen as a win in Taiwan, where fears he might go off script and say something to inadvertently shift the US’ position on the island were high going into the summit.

“US policy on the issue of Taiwan is unchanged as of today and as of the meeting that we had here today,” US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said. “It was raised. They always raised it on their side. We always make clear our position and we move on to other topics.”

But China has made its position clear; the US’ ongoing support for Taiwan could jeopardise one of its most important trade relationships.

The US approved a US$15b ($2.09b) arms package for Taiwan in December last year; its largest ever. But with Trump still yet to give his final approval, its delivery had been stalled.

Whether or not those weapons finally reach Taiwan may be the first real test of whether Xi’s threat made an impact.

While the summit was largely cordial, there were moments that signalled the balance of power between the two leaders might be shifting.

Xi rolled out the red carpet and did a lot to make Trump feel respected; sending his Vice President to greet him at the airport, personally accompanying him on a tour of the Temple of Heaven, and allowing him to visit the highly secretive Zhongnanhai compound, where he and other senior Chinese Communist...
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普称赞这是“有史以来规模最大的峰会”。事实上，他在中国度过的不到48个小时的奢华时光并没有取得什么成果。 对任何真正突破的期望总是很低。但我们在这次高风险峰会上看到的情况仍可能影响未来数月乃至数年的美中关系。 几周来，中国一直在暗示台湾将是此次峰会的首要任务。 该岛的地位一直是美国和中国政府之间的冲突点。中国声称它是一个自治省，最终将受到其控制，而美国长期以来一直是其最大的武器供应商，以防止这种情况发生。 但本周，中国国家主席习近平更进一步；明确表示，今后美中关系最重要的因素将是美国如何对待台湾。 根据中国外交部的讲义，习近平对特朗普说：“台湾问题是中美关系中最重要的问题。” “如果处理得当，双边关系将保持总体稳定。如果处理不好，两国就会发生冲突甚至冲突，使整个美中关系处于极其危险的境地。” 当天晚些时候，当被问及他对事件的看法时，特朗普选择什么也不说。他的沉默在台湾被视为一种胜利，在峰会上，人们非常担心他可能会脱离剧本，说出一些无意中改变美国在台湾的立场的话。 美国国务卿卢比奥表示：“截至今天以及我们今天在这里举行的会议，美国在台湾问题上的政策没有变化。” “有人提出了。他们总是站在自己一边提出。我们总是明确我们的立场，然后转向其他话题。” 但中方已经明确表明立场，美国对台湾的持续支持可能会危及其最重要的贸易关系之一。 去年 12 月，美国批准了一项价值 150 亿美元（2.09b 美元）的台湾军售计划；其规模有史以来最大。但由于特朗普尚未给予最终批准，其交付已陷入停滞。 这些武器最终是否到达台湾可能是习近平的威胁是否产生影响的第一个真正考验。 尽管这次峰会基本上是友好的，但有些时刻表明两位领导人之间的权力平衡可能正在发生变化。 习近平铺上红地毯，做了很多让特朗普感到受到尊重的事情；派副总统到机场迎接他，亲自陪同他游览天坛，并允许他参观高度保密的中南海大院，他和其他中共高级官员都在那里……

reflection.en: News of shifting power dynamics between nations reminds us that human authority is ultimately transient. Psalm 75:7 offers a profound perspective, reminding us that it is God who judges, lifting up one and bringing down another. This truth invites us to look beyond temporary political tides and trust in a higher, unchanging sovereignty.
reflection.zh: 国家间权力动态的变化提醒我们，人类的权威终究是暂时的。诗篇75:7提供了一个深刻的视角，提醒我们是雅伟施行审判，他使这人降卑，使那人升高。这一真理邀请我们超越暂时的政治潮流，信靠那至高无上、永不改变的主权。

verse.textEn: It is God who judges: He brings one down, he exalts another.
verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

title.en: Pakistan faces pressure over mediator role in Iran war
title.zh: 巴基斯坦因在伊朗战争中的调解角色面临压力

summary.en: Pakistan is navigating a complex geopolitical landscape, balancing relationships with Washington, Tehran, Beijing, and key Gulf allies as it takes on a mediator role in a major regional conflict. Recent reports have intensified scrutiny on Islamabad's delicate position.
summary.zh: 巴基斯坦正在复杂的全球地缘政治格局中斡旋，在华盛顿、德黑兰、北京和主要海湾盟友之间寻求平衡，因为它在一个主要的地区冲突中扮演调解角色。最近的媒体报道加剧了对伊斯兰堡微妙立场的审视。

body.en:
With Pakistan stepping in the middle of a major geopolitical conflict, Islamabad is forced to balance between Washington, Tehran, Beijing and key Gulf allies. A recent US media report places it under even more scrutiny.

Pakistan has taken on a leading role in the peace efforts between the US and Iran , hosting talks and serving as an intermediary for backchannel diplomacy between the warring parties .

For Islamabad, the stakes are high. Officials view stability in the Gulf as closely tied to the country's own economic and security interests. A broader confrontation between the US and Iran could disrupt trade routes, deepen energy pressures, inflame sectarian tensions and further destabilize Pakistan's sensitive border regions with Iran.

International prestige is also at play for the Pakistani government as they work to end a conflict affecting the entire world . But this also means a risk of reputational damage.

"Pakistan risks growing criticism if its efforts to revive US-Iran talks fail, especially after publicly taking a leading mediation role," Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow for South Asia at the Washington-based Atlantic Council, told DW. 

"With talks stalled, Pakistan's options are limited because a mediator cannot force two deeply distrustful sides to negotiate," he added.

"Pakistan is trying its best to engage both parties and views the escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran with grave concern," a senior government official involved in the negotiation process told DW. 

"We are committed to playing a constructive diplomatic role to support immediate de-escalation and a peaceful resolution in the interest of regional and global security," the official added. 

Earlier this week, a report in US media raised doubt over Pakistan's neutrality in the Iran conflict. Citing unnamed US officials, CBS News reported that Pakistan had allowed Iran to park its aircraft on Pakistani airbases , effectively shielding them from US strikes.

Pakistan's Foreign Office immediately responded by calling the report "misleading" and "speculative." In an official statement, Islamabad said the aircraft activity was linked to diplomatic and logistical arrangements connected to ongoing peace efforts and involved personnel from multiple sides.

The Foreign Office also warned that "unverified and sensationalized reporting" risked undermining sensitive diplomatic initiatives.

US Senator Lindsey Graham, an outspoken supporter of the US war in Iran, publicly criticized Pakistan following the CBS report.
